skill.name: arch-view
skill.description: Generate architecture views from Backstage catalog-info.yaml metadata, including dependency graphs, request flows, event topology, and service groupings.
skill.summary: Visualize service architecture from repository catalog metadata.
skill.author: AstraBit-CPT

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, Mermaid syntax, architecture terminology, and a normal YAML parser variable named key. The skill does document real external command usage for GitHub discovery and bundled Python scripts, which should require user confirmation because they read repository metadata and may write output files.

remediation.issue: Documented external CLI commands can access local repositories or GitHub metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running gh repo list or bundled Python scripts, and show the exact command and target path first.

remediation.issue: Generated Mermaid labels and node identifiers are built from repository metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize component names, route labels, and topic names before placing them in Mermaid output.

remediation.issue: Optional GitHub discovery is tied to a hardcoded organization name.
remediation.suggestion: Make the organization explicit in the user prompt and support an override instead of silently using a fixed value.

content.value_statement: Large service portfolios are hard to understand from scattered repository metadata. This skill turns catalog files into dependency, request flow, event, and grouping views.
actual_capabilities: Collects Backstage-style catalog-info.yaml metadata from repository directories.
Aggregates components, dependencies, domains, owners, routes, and event topics.
Generates Mermaid service dependency graphs from declared dependsOn relationships.
Builds request flow maps from gateway routes and downstream service dependencies.
Creates event topology diagrams for declared producers, consumers, and topics.
Produces Markdown service grouping tables by domain, type, and owner.
limitations: Requires useful catalog-info.yaml files in the target repositories.
Shows declared architecture metadata, not live runtime traffic or production state.
Optional GitHub discovery needs GitHub CLI access and explicit user approval.
Generated diagrams may need cleanup when metadata names contain unsupported Mermaid syntax.

use_cases.title: Map service dependencies
use_cases.description: Create a readable dependency graph from repository metadata before a platform migration or technical review.

use_cases.title: Explain request paths
use_cases.description: Show how external requests move through gateways and services for onboarding or incident analysis.

use_cases.title: Review event ownership
use_cases.description: Identify producers, consumers, and topics to support event-driven architecture planning.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic architecture view
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a complete overview.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an architecture view from the repositories in repos/. Include the summary, dependency graph, request flow, event topology, and missing metadata list.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: User needs a service dependency diagram only.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read catalog-info.yaml files under repos/ and create a Mermaid service dependency graph. Highlight gateways, services, workers, databases, and libraries.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze request and event flows
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of traffic and messaging.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build request flow and event topology views from the repository metadata. Explain which gateway routes, topics, producers, and consumers are represented.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an architecture review pack
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cross-repository review for decision makers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Aggregate all available catalog metadata, generate every architecture view, group services by domain and owner, and list metadata gaps that affect confidence.

output_examples.input: Generate a full architecture view for repos/.
output: A summary of total repositories, components with metadata, and missing metadata.
A service dependency diagram showing gateways, services, workers, libraries, and databases.
Request flow and event topology sections when route and event metadata exists.
Domain and type grouping tables for service ownership review.

output_examples.input: Show only the event topology for the trading domain.
output: A focused event topology view for trading services.
Producer and consumer relationships grouped by topic.
Notes about missing event metadata that limits the view.

output_examples.input: Which repositories are missing catalog metadata?
output_examples.output: A concise missing metadata section listing repositories without catalog-info.yaml and explaining how that affects diagram coverage.

best_practices: Review the target repository directory before running aggregation commands.
Ask for user approval before using GitHub CLI discovery or writing output files.
Treat generated diagrams as metadata-based drafts and verify them with service owners.
anti_patterns: Do not run GitHub CLI discovery without explaining the organization and credentials used.
Do not present diagrams as runtime truth when they only reflect catalog metadata.
Do not include private architecture diagrams in public issue trackers or shared chats.

faq.question: What metadata format does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects Backstage-style catalog-info.yaml files with component, dependency, route, domain, owner, and event metadata.

faq.question: Can it scan live services?
faq.answer: No. It reads repository metadata and does not inspect live infrastructure, traffic, or deployed service state.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub access?
faq.answer: No for local repositories. Optional repository discovery uses GitHub CLI and should require user approval.

faq.question: What diagram format does it generate?
faq.answer: It generates Mermaid diagrams and Markdown tables that can be rendered or edited in supported tools.

faq.question: What happens when metadata is missing?
faq.answer: The skill lists missing catalog files and omits those repositories from architecture diagrams.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
